selectionCriteria.provenance: Three tasks under bench/corpus/tui-games/, one directory each. The two headless tasks hold a normative SPEC.md - the rules, the constants, the generator definitions, the merge table and the recorded conformance vectors - beside a seed/ the arm works in and a gauge/ it never sees. snake-tui-cpp holds a normative SPEC.md and an EMPTY seed: there is no partial implementation to complete, so the specification carries the whole contract and the arm chooses everything the specification does not pin. None of the three is self-graded: a game task scored by comparing a tree against output that same tree was told to produce has a metric that cannot fail, and there is no such metric in this set. Expected output comes from a reference implementation validated against the specification's own pins, which for snake-tui-cpp is checked in under reference/.
selectionCriteria.whyOnlyTwo: Eight tui-games tasks exist and six are not here, and bench/corpus/DEFERRED.md names them one by one with what each would need. A tui-games task is scored by the model's own test.sh comparing the model's output against expected files the same model was told to generate, so the corpus's defence against that is a cross-language majority vote over five languages plus a human reviewer - neither of which a one-language headless cell has. An authored hidden gauge is only honest when the specification pins enough ground truth to prove the gauge itself right, and only snake and 2048 pin that much. snake-tui-cpp is the third task because it reuses snake's already-proved rules and adds the half the other two decline to measure, not because a third game was found.
selectionCriteria.whatIsMeasured: For the two headless tasks, the pure rules half only: no terminal, no raw mode, no signal handling, no pacing, no flicker and no idle-CPU budget. Roughly a third of the corpus's own snake rubric - terminal hygiene and loop discipline - is unmeasurable in a headless cell and is not measured there. snake-tui-cpp measures it, because a pseudo-terminal can drive what a pipe cannot: seven of its thirty-six checks spawn the real binary on a real terminal device and read what was drawn - the alternate screen entered and left, a forty-cell row actually rendered, the head moving in the direction the key names, the turn rule refusing a reversal at the front end too, a status line, a pause indicator, a clean exit on q and on end of input, and a terminal too small getting a message rather than a broken frame. Idle CPU and flicker remain unmeasured everywhere.
selectionCriteria.scopeLadder: T2 and T3, one and two tasks. grid2048-headless-py names two independent requirements in two files that share nothing, which is the disjoint-scope shape T2 names. snake-headless-py is a four-module chain where each module imports the one before it, which is the shape T3 names. snake-tui-cpp is the same chain shape reached from an empty tree: a rules core, then two front ends over it, plus the build script without which nothing else can be checked. T0, T1 and T4 are empty and the pin says so.
selectionCriteria.hiddenTests: The measurement lives in gauge/, which is never seeded into the work tree and is materialized only after the model's process has exited. Every expectation in it is either pinned by the seeded specification or produced by a reference implementation validated against those pins; nothing is compared against the work tree's own recorded output, which is the failure mode the corpus's own acceptance notes call out by name.
selectionCriteria.seedIsGreen: The two headless seeds pass their own visible suite, so a run starts from a green tree and a red visible test is the arm's doing. grid2048-headless-py additionally keeps its visible suite green once both requirements are met, which was checked against a complete implementation rather than assumed. snake-tui-cpp starts RED and cannot do otherwise: its visible suite builds the program first, and on an empty tree there is no build.sh to run. It fails with that sentence, which is the honest state of a workspace with no program in it - and it is the red half of the red-green a from-scratch task begins with.
selectionCriteria.languageMix: python for the two headless tasks, C++ for snake-tui-cpp. The headless pair are pure logic over integers and lists with no build step; snake-tui-cpp has a build step ON PURPOSE, because how an arm chooses to build - one c++ invocation, a Makefile, CMake and Ninja - is part of what the three arms are being compared on. The corpus's five-language list exists to feed the cross-language vote this campaign does not run.
selectionCriteria.preAnsweredMaterial: Each seed's SPEC.md carries the specification's own worked examples, and the hidden gauge asserts some of them: the two generator sequences, the three first-food cells and the 1061-byte summary line for both snakes; the three generator vector rows, the five initial boards and the twelve-row merge table for 2048. Removing them would gut the normative document the task is built against. The recorded replay vectors - which is where each gauge's discrimination actually lives - appear nowhere in any seed, and neither does anything about the terminal half beyond the requirements themselves.

sweep.rationale: One model, because one model is served. The set holds one T2 and one T3 task, so the two tiers that have a task in them are the swept ones and every other tier is primary-only by vacuity.

tasks.expectedTrajectory: the run decomposes to two independent items - the merge rule in src/moves.py and the rewind in src/undo.py - with disjoint fileScopes, and the scheduler dispatches them in one wave
tasks.rationale: Two named requirements, two files, no shared edit: neither module imports the other and src/session.py calls into both without either knowing the other exists, so the wave scheduler has two dependency-ready items with disjoint scopes and can dispatch them together. The gate is calibrated rather than assumed - on the unmodified seed 14 of the 24 graded cases fail, implementing only the merge rule leaves 7 failing, implementing only the rewind leaves 13 failing, and implementing both leaves none - so a cell passes exactly when both blocks are right and nothing else regressed.
tasks.prompt:
This workspace holds a headless 2048, specified by SPEC.md. The generator, the board, the spawn protocol, the counters, the script parser, the replay loop and the summary are written and pass the visible suite. Two requirements are not implemented, and NOTES.md keeps the index of which is where:

- R7 step 2, in src/moves.py: slide_left gathers a row's non-zero values and pads the row back to four, but never combines a pair, so it emits every tile it was given and always reports a gain of zero. SPEC.md section 5 has the rule and the twelve-row table it has to satisfy. src/moves.py already routes all four directions through slide_left, so the rule lands once for all of them.
- R13 and R14, in src/undo.py: a snapshot carries the board and the score only. The move counter and the generator's state are not recorded and not restored, so `moves` keeps climbing across an undo and a direction replayed after an undo draws fresh numbers and spawns a different tile. CAPACITY is declared and not enforced, so the stack grows without bound.

Implement both. They touch different files and neither depends on the other. Do not regress anything that already works: the specification is normative in full, and the graded run checks the merge table row by row and column by column, move legality and rejection, the score, the rewind, and whole recorded summary lines byte for byte including the generator's state word.

python3 tools/run_tests.py tests must keep passing. Keep NOTES.md honest: its requirement index is the workspace's own account of itself, so a requirement that stops being unimplemented moves in that table too.

Do not change src/rng.py, src/board.py, src/summary.py, src/session.py or src/replay.py. Do not special-case an input by its values, its length or the seed it came from.

tasks.expectedTrajectory: the run decomposes to items chained rng -> food -> engine -> replay, producing three or more waves, with each later item held until the one it imports publishes
tasks.rationale: A four-module chain that cannot be reordered: food placement indexes a generator draw, the game consumes a placement per growth tick, and the replay drives the game from a fixed directive list. The graded run drives it with recorded scripts and compares whole summaries, so an arm that welds the rules into the replay loop still passes and an arm that gets the draw order wrong does not. Every expectation in the gauge was proved against a reference implementation written from the seeded specification alone, which reproduced the two pinned generator sequences, the three pinned first-food cells and the 1061-byte worked example byte for byte.
tasks.prompt:
This workspace holds a headless game of Snake, specified by SPEC.md. There is no terminal in it anywhere: a seed and a script of directives go in, one line of JSON comes out, and the same two inputs always produce the same bytes.

src/board.py and src/summary.py are written. Four modules are not, and each one needs the one before it:

1. src/rng.py exports Lcg. Lcg(seed) sets the state to seed modulo 2**32 and next() advances it by the multiplier and increment SPEC.md section 4 pins. Both sequences in that section must reproduce.
2. src/food.py exports place(snake, rng). It indexes the free cells - src.board.free_cells already produces them in the order the placement depends on - with exactly one draw, and returns None on a full board.
3. src/engine.py exports Game, per SPEC.md section 5: the initial state, the direction rule, pause, the tick with its wall, self and growth cases, the win condition, and restart.
4. src/replay.py exports ScriptError, parse, replay and fields, per SPEC.md sections 6 to 8.

Do not change src/board.py or src/summary.py, and keep the rules out of src/replay.py: the replay applies directives and nothing else.

python3 tools/run_tests.py tests must keep passing. The graded run drives recorded scripts the workspace does not contain and compares whole summaries, so a partial field check is worth nothing there.

Nothing may sleep, read the wall clock, read a real random source, or open a socket. Do not special-case a script or a seed by its bytes, its length or its value.

tasks.expectedTrajectory: the run decomposes to a rules core, a headless front end over it and a terminal front end over it, plus the build script every other item needs to be checkable at all, so the two front ends are dependency-ready together once the core publishes
tasks.rationale: The first from-scratch task in the corpus and the first that scores a TUI. Every other task seeds a partial implementation and names the gaps; this one seeds a specification and an empty tree, so what an arm BUILDS - the layout, the build system, whether it draws with escape sequences or links ncurses - is chosen rather than inherited, which is the comparison the three arms exist to make and which no fill-the-gaps task can produce. It also closes the gap this manifest's own whatIsMeasured records: 'neither task claims to score a TUI', because a headless cell cannot. A pseudo-terminal can. Seven of the thirty-six checks spawn the real binary on a real terminal device, send keystrokes and read what was drawn. The gate is calibrated rather than assumed: a complete reference implementation under reference/ runs the whole gauge green in about seven seconds, and twenty-two single-edit mutations of that reference were each caught - the generator multiplier (17 checks), the food index (18), turning against the pending direction instead of the committed one (1), a restart that does not re-seed (1), a restart honoured while alive (1), a tick counted while paused (1), the score per food (4), a wall collision that moves the snake (3), a growth tick that drops the tail (4), a summary without its newline (19), a script error exiting 0 (6), a missing alternate-screen enter (1) and leave (2), a missing Score line (1) and PAUSED (1), q exiting non-zero (1), wasd ignored (1), the arrow keys ignored (1), a board never drawn (6), a board drawn into a thirty-column terminal (2), an ignored end of input (1), and a --tick-ms 0 that never ticks (3). Expected output is the reference's, never the work tree's own.
tasks.prompt:
This workspace holds a specification and an empty tree. Build the program SPEC.md describes: a game of Snake in C++ with two front ends over one set of rules — a terminal game a person plays, and a headless mode that runs a script of directives and prints one line of JSON.

SPEC.md is normative in full. Three things at the outside of the program are fixed, because the graded run drives them and nothing else:

- `./build.sh` builds the program, takes no arguments, exits 0, and leaves an executable `./snake` at the root of the work tree. It must work twice in a row.
- `./snake --headless --seed <n> --script <path>` prints exactly one line of JSON to stdout and exits 0. A script that violates section 8 exits 3 with nothing on stdout. Section 9 pins the sixteen keys, their order, and a 1061-byte worked example.
- `./snake` plays on the terminal: the alternate screen, raw input, the arrow keys and `wasd` to turn, `p` to pause, `r` to restart, `q` to quit with status 0, a status line carrying `Score:`, and a message rather than a broken frame when the terminal is too small.

Everything else is yours, and deliberately so: the file layout, the class design, the build system, whether you draw with raw escape sequences or link the system ncurses, and how you divide the work. There is no required directory, no required file and no required class. One translation unit compiled by one `c++` invocation satisfies this specification as fully as a CMake project with several targets.

The machine has Apple Clang with C++23, CMake, Ninja and the system ncurses (`-lncurses`, `<curses.h>`). There is no network, so a dependency fetched at build time will fail the build.

`tools/run_tests.sh` is the visible suite: it builds, then runs every executable directly under `tests/`. On a fresh checkout it fails because there is no `build.sh` yet, and it fails when there are no tests at all — a suite that runs nothing is not a passing suite. Write the tests you need under `tests/`.

The graded run executes the built binary and never reads your source: recorded scripts across four seeds, compared byte for byte, and the terminal game driven under a pseudo-terminal. The headless mode must not sleep, read the wall clock, read a real random source, or open a socket. Do not special-case a script or a seed by its bytes, its length or its value.
